  CONCURRENT JOINT MEETINGS OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  COMMERCE, JOINT POWERS FINANCING AUTHORITY AND THE GOVERNING BODY
  OF THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE COMMERCE COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT
  COMMISSION
To protect public health, this meeting is being held in accordance with AB 361, Government
Code section 54954(e)(1) (A). Given the proclaimed state of emergency and the Los Angeles
County Health Department recommendation for social distancing for public meetings, which is
also consistent with Cal OSHA requirements for social distancing, the City will be conducting
public meetings via video/teleconferencing and there will be no physical location available for
this meeting. To participate in the City of Commerce ‘public meetings and provide public
comment during the COVID-19 public health emergency, please follow these steps:
1. Watch or Listen: Meetings are broadcast/streamed live on the City of Commerce’s
Facebook:  https://www.facebook.com/City-of-Commerce-123903054365151/?ref.  Archived,
on-demand video of each meeting is maintained on the City’s Facebook as part of the public
record.

2. Submit Comments before the Meeting: Members of the public can provide public comment
by sending an e-mail to cityclerk@ci.commerce.ca.us for City Council meetings, and the
comment will be read during Public Comment portion.

3. Live Remote Public Comments: Members of the public may submit live public comment via
Zoom conferencing by using the link below. You must download the Zoom app or software.
Zoom meetings can be accessed by telephone, computer, or smart device. You will be allowed
to speak during Public Comment portion of the agenda.

4.  At the time and date of the meeting, please click this URL to join the Zoom meeting:

https://us06web.zoom.us/j/85859254654?pwd=c0had1pIVkFjMVJwZ2VHYmwwaVdSUT09

Passcode: 453322 or join by phone: Dial 1(720) 707-2699; Meeting ID: 858 5925 4654

5. To listen to the meeting in Spanish or speak under Public Comment in Spanish, please click
this URL to join the Zoom meeting via Spanish:

https://us06web.zoom.us/j/85156940336?pwd=Z0hjV1pLYjBXMzR1OXROTkdhcDJSdz09

  CONSENT CALENDAR
Items under the Consent Calendar are considered to be routine and may be enacted by one motion. There will be
no discussion of these items unless members of the Public or City Council request specific items to be removed
from the Consent Agenda for a separate discussion. lf the item is desired to be discussed separately, it should be
the first item under Scheduled Matters.

4.  Approval of Warrant Register Nos. 13A, & 13B
  The City Council and Successor Agency will consider for approval the bills and
  claims set forth in Warrant Registers No. 13A, dated February 22, 2022 and
  13B dated February 9, 2022 through February 16, 2022.
  Attachments:  13 A 2022
  13 B 2022

5.  Approval of Minutes
  The City Council and Successor Agency will consider for approval the minutes
  of the Regular City Council meeting of Tuesday, February 8, 2022, the minutes
  of the Regular City Council meeting of Tuesday, January 25, 2022, held at
  5:00 p.m., the minutes of the Special City Council meeting of Monday,
  November 29, 2021, held at 5:00 p.m., and the minutes of the Special City
  Council meeting of Monday, January 31, 2022, held at 5:00 p.m.
  Attachments:  2022-02-08 CC Minutes
  2022-01-31 CC Minutes
  2021-11-29 CC Minutes
  2022-01-25 CC Minutes

6.  Opposition to State Ballot Measure Initiative 21-0026A1 Restricting Voter’s
  Input and Local Taxing Authority
  The City Council will consider for adoption a Resolution affirming the City's
  opposition to Initiative 21-0026A1, a State ballot measure restricting voters'
  input and local taxing authority.
  Attachments:  Staff Report
  Resolution
  League of CA Cities Analysis
  CBRT Fiscal Analysis

7.  Letter of Opposition to Los Angeles County Mask Mandate
  The City Council will consider approval a letter of opposition to Los Angeles
  County's decision to continue to uphold a mask mandate beyond the State's
  repeal of such on February 15, 2022.
  Attachments:  Staff Report
  Oppose Mask Mandate Letter

8.  First Amendment to the Agreement for City Attorney Services with
  Alvarez-Glasman & Colvin
  The City Council will consider approving the First Amendment to the
  Agreement for City Attorney Services with Alvarez-Glasman & Colvin adjusting
  rates for legal services.
  Attachments:  Staff Report
  First Amendment

9.  Professional Services Agreement with Hartzog & Grabill, Inc. for the
  Preparation of Mixmaster Guide Signage Improvements Plans,
  Specification and Engineer’s Estimate
  The City Council will consider for adoption a Resolution awarding a
  Professional Services Agreement to Hartzog & Crabill, Inc. for the preparation
  of Mixmaster Guide Signage Improvement Plans, Specifications and Engineer's
  Estimate and authorizing Project Management Services by Transtech
  Engineers.
  Attachments:  Staff Report
  Resolution
  PSA- HCI.

  Rehabilitation Project and Authorize Staff to Advertise the Notice Inviting
  Bids
  The City Council will consider for adoption a Resolution approving  the
  construction project plans, specifications, and estimates for the FY 2021/2022
  Pavement Rehabilitation Project and authorize staff to advertise the Notice
  Inviting Bids.
  Attachments:  Staff Report
  Resolution

  Concept Layout for the New Commerce City Hall Facilities
  The City Council will consider for adoption a Resolution awarding a
  Professional Services Agreement to IDS Group to prepare conceptual layouts
  for the New City Hall Facilities and authorizing Project Management Services
  by Transtech Engineers.

  Resolution
  PSA IDS Group

  and Everington Street

  Resolution

13.  Weed Abatement Program - Abatement Order Directing the Los Angeles
  County Agricultural Commissioners/Director of Weights and Measures to
  Abate Public Nuisance
  The City Council will consider approving the Abatement Order directing the
  Los Angeles County Agricultural Commissioner/Director of Weights and
  Measures to abate the public nuisance, and allow those property owners
  affected by the Weed Abatement Program to protest the inclusion of their
  properties within the program.
  Attachments:  Staff Report
  22-19 Weed Abatement
  Declaration

14.  I-5/Atlantic Blvd Over Crossing Bridge Widening Project Development
  Process and Rough Order of Magnitude Cost Estimate
  The City Council will receive and file an informational presentation on the
  I-5/Atlantic Blvd Over Crossing Bridge Widening Project Development Process
  and Rough Order of Magnitude Cost Estimate that was prompted by a
  previous City Council discussion related to a request for traffic relief at the
  subject site.
  Attachments:  Staff Report.docx

15.  Second Reading and Adoption by Waiving the Full Reading and Reading
  by Title Only of an Ordinance to (A) Approve Specific Plan No. 21-01, (B)
  Approve Zone Change 21-01, Consisting of Amendments to Title 19 of
  the Commerce Municipal Code (“Zoning”) to Amend Section 19.05.010
  Zones Established, Establish a New Section 19.16, Specific Plans, and
  Amend Section 19.25.140, Off-Site Signs Permitted with Restrictions, and
  Approve an Associated Amendment to the Zoning Map to Designate the
  Site of the Modelo Specific Plan (Specific Plan No. 21-01), and (C)
  Approve a Development Agreement Associated with the Modelo Project
  The City Council will consider for second reading and adoption by waiving the
  full reading, and reading by title only an Ordinance (A) approving Specific Plan
  No. 21-01, (B) approving Zone Change 21-01, consisting of amendments to
  Title 19 of the CMC ("ZONING") to amend Section 19.05.010 Zones
  Established, establishing a new Section 19.16 Specific Plans, and amending
  Section 19.25.140, Off-Site Signs permitted with restrictions, and approval of
  an associated amendment to the Zoning Map to designate the site of the
  Modelo Specific Plan (SPECIFIC PLAN NO. 21-01), and (C) approving a
  development agreement associated with the Modelo Project.

16.  Adoption and Second Reading by Waiving Full Reading and Reading by
  Title Only, of an Uncodified Ordinance Approving Amended and Restated
  Development Agreement Related to Application #18-074 and Replacing
  Commercial Cannabis Development Agreements No. 724
  The City Council will consider for Second Reading and Adoption, by waiving
  the full reading and reading by title only, an Uncodified Ordinance approving
  an amended and restated Development Agreement the Green City LLC.,
  Commercial Cannabis related to Permit Application No. 18-074, and to replace
  Development Agreement No. 724 for expanding of square footage within the
  existing building, and change of name of business, for a commercial cannabis
  business at 2939 S. Vail Ave.
  Attachments:  Staff Report
  Development Agreement Green City
  Ordinance Green City

17.  Adoption and Second Reading by Waiving Full Reading and Reading by
  Title Only, of an Uncodified Ordinance Approving an Amended and
  Restated Development Agreement Related to Application #18-027 and
  Replacing Commercial Cannabis Development Agreement No. No. 727
  The City Council will consider for Adoption and Second Reading, by waiving
  the full reading and reading by title only, an Uncodified Ordinance approving
  an amended and restated Development Agreement with ABC Commerce, LLC
  related to Commercial Cannabis Permit Application No. 18-027, and to replace
  Development Agreement No. 727 for changing ownership of an approved
  commercial cannabis business at 6915 E. Slauson Ave.
  Attachments:  Staff Report
  ABC Cmmerce - Development Agreement
  ABC Commerce - Ordinance

CITY COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY REPORTS

ADJOURNMENT
Written materials distributed to the City Council are available for public inspection immediately
following the posting of this agenda (at least 72 hours prior to a regular City Council meetings)
in the City Clerk's Office, at Commerce City Hall, 2535 Commerce Way, Commerce, California,
and via the City's website.
If requested, the agenda and backup materials will be made available in appropriate alternative
formats to persons with a disability, as required by Section 202 of the Americans with
Disabilities Act of 1990 (42 U.S.C. Sec. 12132), and the federal rules and regulations adopted in
implementation thereof.  Any person who requires a disability-related modification or
accommodation, in order to observe and/or offer public comment may request such
reasonable modification, accommodation, aid, or service by contacting via email to
cityclerk@ci.commerce.ca.us or by telephone at 323-722-4805 no later than 9 AM on the day of
the scheduled meeting.
